claims.text: Forming a protective oxide layer on a high-entropy alloy can reduce its coefficient of friction relative to the untreated alloy.
Forming a protective oxide layer on a high-entropy alloy can reduce its wear rate relative to the untreated alloy.
The reductions in friction and wear can persist across a wide service-temperature range, including elevated temperatures.
The protective oxide layer prevents direct metal-to-metal contact between the alloy and the counterface.
The protective oxide layer reduces adhesion between the alloy and the counterface.
Preventing direct metal-to-metal contact and reducing adhesion lower the coefficient of friction.
Preventing direct metal-to-metal contact and reducing adhesion lower the wear rate.
The effectiveness of the intervention is bounded by temperature range, alloy composition, and oxide-layer formation.
The exact mechanism of protective-oxide formation and its effect on alloy properties and behavior is not fully understood.
